localChanges: New games and saved games now record which map grid the world is on, ready for isometric and hex maps. Nothing changes on screen yet, and games saved before this load as square, as they always have (closes #89).

log: The `start` rule reads the engine option `topologyId` (default `'square'`) and passes it to the generator as its `topologyId` option, which core-world-generator 0.1.7's `Generator.topology()` resolves through core-world's `createTopology` at the generator's final size; `World` 0.1.21 records the id from there.

Before generating, it validates the generator's own topology against the generator's own `width()` and `height()`, so an unknown id or a size the grid cannot make (an odd height on `staggered-iso` or `hex-odd-r`, which always wrap north to south) throws before any terrain is generated, rather than from inside `World`. Earth's maps are square data, so the `earth` option with any other `topologyId` throws an `Error` naming both, before a generator is picked.
Square worlds are unchanged: the generator's default grid is already square. core-world is now `^0.1.21` and core-world-generator `^0.1.7` (web-renderer#89).

Compile with `--force`, format as `npm run build` does, and fail if any `.js`, `.d.ts` or `.js.map` then differs from what is committed or was never added, as core-world-generator and simple-world-generator already do.

`Game.inject` rebuilt a loaded `World`'s transient `_generator` as a plain `new Generator(height, width)`, so its `topology()` was always square. With core-world 0.1.21 a world saves its grid as `_topologyId`, and with core-world-generator 0.1.7 a `Generator` takes a `topologyId` option, so the rebuild now passes `{ topologyId: target._topologyId ?? 'square' }` and the generator's `topology()`, `getNeighbours` and `distanceFrom` agree with the world it belongs to (civ-clone/web-renderer#89).

The id is read from the restored field, like the height and width. A world saved before ids were recorded has none when `fill` runs (`World.onHydrated`, which gives it `'square'`, runs afterwards), so its generator is square, as it always was. Nothing reads a loaded world's generator geometry today (`World.get` uses only `coordsToIndex`), so square worlds behave exactly as before; the comment above the rebuild no longer claims the geometry is a function of height and width alone.

The dependency ranges move to core-world ^0.1.21 and core-world-generator ^0.1.7, the first versions with `World._topologyId` and the `topologyId` option. Three inject tests: a loaded world saved as `'hex-odd-r'` gets a hex generator of its own size whose neighbours are the world topology's; a world saved without the field gets a square one; and no transient field of the world is left undefined.

`PlayerWorld` gains a `topologyId()` accessor, delegating to `World.topologyId()` (core-world 0.1.21), and a `topologyId` key, so the data a client is sent says which grid the world is on (civ-clone/web-renderer#89). The client never receives the `World` itself, only the player's view of it.

A save carries each object's keys beside its state, so a game saved before this would restore its `PlayerWorld`s without the key, never send it, and write the same keys into every later save. `onHydrated` adds the key when it is missing; `World` reports `'square'` for such a world.

core-world is now `^0.1.21`, for `World.topologyId()` and `TopologyId`. The package gets its first tests (mocha/chai/ts-mocha, as core-world's): the key is sent and reads `'square'` for a default world and `'hex-odd-r'`/`'staggered-iso'` for worlds whose generator was given those topologies, and a `PlayerWorld` restored with the old keys sends it after `onHydrated` (once, however often that runs).

The workflow is the standard one the other engine repos now use: pnpm on Node 22 with no lock file, `prettier --check`, a forced compile that fails on stale or uncommitted `.js`/`.d.ts`/`.js.map`, then the tests.

`prettier:check` gains `--check`: without it, it printed every file formatted and passed whatever their state. The unused `package-lock.json` (npm v2 lock from 0.1.13's era, pinning core-data-object 0.1.9 and no test tooling) is removed; CI resolves what a consumer would.
ITopology gains id(), returning a TopologyId: 'square', 'staggered-iso' or 'hex-odd-r'. These are written into saved games (web-renderer#89), so they are never renamed or reused.

topologies.ts exports createTopology(id, width, height), which builds and validates the topology an id names and throws a clear Error for an id it does not know, and topologyIds, the list. It is pure, so the UI can use it too. The staggered and hexagonal grids are always built to wrap north to south, as World.get does whatever the grid, so an odd height is refused for them rather than quietly making a world that does not wrap; square takes any size of at least 1 by 1.

A World takes the id of its generator's topology when it is built and keeps it in _topologyId, a saved (non-transient) field, with a topologyId() accessor. topology() is now built lazily from that id and the dimensions through createTopology, and is still transient and reset in onHydrated.
A world saved before the id was recorded has none: onHydrated makes it 'square', the only grid there was, so the next save records it.

A generator's topology from a copy of core-world older than id() (two copies exist whenever core-world-generator's core-world does not match, as in this package's own CI install) counts as square. The core-world-generator range is raised to ^0.1.6, the first with Generator.topology().

For a square world nothing plays differently. The one change a save shows is the new field: web-renderer's conformance state digest gains one field per checkpoint, and is otherwise unchanged (web-renderer#89).

A topology from a copy of core-world older than id() used to count as square whatever it was. That copy (0.1.20) already has StaggeredIsoTopology and HexOddRTopology, so one of those injected into a generator would have been saved as square. Class identity cannot be compared across copies, so the fallback now goes by class name: a SquareTopology, a generator's default, is still recorded as square, and anything else throws an Error naming the class and saying core-world-generator's copy of core-world predates topology ids.

`Object.freeze([dx, dy] as [number, number])` comes out as `readonly number[]` under TypeScript 4.8, which several engine checkouts pin, so `offset()`'s `Offset` return type rejected it (TS2322 in 20 checkouts' typecheck). `Object.freeze<[number, number]>([dx, dy])` is a readonly tuple on 4.8 and 4.9 alike. The compiled JavaScript is unchanged; only the source maps move.

`new Generator(height, width, { topologyId })` names the grid by id ('square' by default). `topology()` builds it lazily with core-world's `createTopology(id, width(), height())`, so it is made at the size the generator really lays out, which a subclass such as civ1-earth-generator's Earth can change from the size it was asked for. An unknown id, or a size the grid cannot wrap, throws createTopology's Error on first use.
An `options.topology` instance (0.1.6) still wins when given. The default square grid is now built through the factory, which also validates its dimensions (at least 1x1).
Needs core-world ^0.1.21 for `topologies`. The test strip topology gains the `id()` and `steps()` that ITopology now requires.
Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#89.

BaseGenerator called `super(height, width)`, so none of its options reached core-world-generator's `Generator`. It now passes them on, so the `topologyId` option (core-world-generator 0.1.7) chooses the grid `topology()` builds; `IOptions` gains `topologyId`. Without one the grid is square, as before, and the seeded maps are unchanged.
core-world-generator is now `^0.1.7`, and core-world (dev) `^0.1.21` for `ITopology.id()` in the tests. Part of civ-clone/web-renderer#89.
